opportunities.title: Binance's $6.3B Hack Is 'Resolved.' Nothing About the Next One Will Be Different.
opportunities.why_now: Binance just completed withdrawal recovery four weeks after history's largest exchange hack, closing the loop on an incident that changed nothing structurally.
opportunities.angle: Post-mortem/op-ed: walk through the timeline, note what Binance actually fixed vs. what it PR'd, and argue custodial risk is a pricing input, not a tail event.

opportunities.title: The Bitcoin Wallet Bug Nobody Found for Five Years (Including the Auditors Who Were Paid To)
opportunities.why_now: Coldcard just disclosed exactly how a flaw in its hardware wallet slipped past years of security reviews — a rare inside look at audit failure, not just exploit aftermath.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive explainer: why audits miss this class of bug, what it means for 'audited = safe' marketing claims across the hardware wallet industry.

opportunities.title: Tether Can Freeze Your Stolen Funds in Minutes. Getting Them Back Takes Years — If Ever.
opportunities.why_now: CoinDesk's reporting lays bare the gap between Tether's freeze speed and the actual legal/operational mess victims face recovering funds, right as Binance victims test that pipeline post-hack.
opportunities.angle: Explainer that debunks 'Tether froze it, crisis averted' headlines — map the real recovery timeline and who actually gets made whole (spoiler: rarely the victim first).

opportunities.title: One Tiny Payment Can Unmask Your Bitcoin Wallet's IP Address — Here's the Trick
opportunities.why_now: A developer just published a method showing how a small transaction can deanonymize a wallet's network location, a fresh privacy-leak vector with no patch consensus yet.
opportunities.angle: Technical breakdown for self-custody users: how the attack works, who's exposed (node operators, Lightning users), and concrete mitigation steps (Tor, Dandelion++, etc.).

opportunities.title: The UK Is Writing DeFi Rules Based on a Hack That Had Nothing to Do With DeFi
opportunities.why_now: The FCA is citing the $6.3B Binance hack — a centralized exchange failure — to justify new DeFi regulation, a telling conflation that will shape policy debates for months.
opportunities.angle: Sharp commentary piece: expose the category error regulators keep making between CeFi custody failures and DeFi protocol risk, and what it means for builders bracing for rules written for the wrong problem.
